senses.definition: (of a law) having legal validity
examples: the law is still in effect

senses.definition: a phenomenon that follows and is caused by some previous phenomenon
examples: the magnetic effect was greater when the rod was lengthwise
his decision had depressing consequences for business
he acted very wise after the event

senses.definition: a symptom caused by an illness or a drug
examples: the effects of sleep loss
the effect of the anesthetic

senses.definition: an impression (especially one that is artificial or contrived)
examples: he just did it for effect

senses.definition: an outward appearance
examples: he made a good impression
I wanted to create an impression of success
she retained that bold effect in her reproductions of the original painting

senses.definition: the central meaning or theme of a speech or literary work
act so as to bring into existence
examples: effect a change

senses.definition: produce
examples: The scientists set up a shock wave

senses.definition: able to accomplish a purpose; functioning effectively
examples: people who will do nothing unless they get something out of it for themselves are often highly effective persons …
effective personnel
an efficient secretary
the efficient cause of the revolution

senses.definition: exerting force or influence
examples: the law is effective immediately
a warranty good for two years
the law is already in effect (or in force)

senses.definition: existing in fact; not theoretical; real
examples: a decline in the effective demand
confused increased equipment and expenditure with the quantity of effective work done

senses.definition: producing or capable of producing an intended result or having a striking effect
examples: an air-cooled motor was more effective than a witch's broomstick for rapid long-distance transportation
effective teaching methods
effective steps toward peace
made an effective entrance
his complaint proved to be effectual in bringing action
an efficacious law

senses.definition: ready for service
examples: the fort was held by about 100 effective soldiers

senses.definition: works well as a means or remedy
examples: an effective reprimand
a lotion that is effective in cases of prickly heat

senses.definition: in actuality or reality or fact
examples: she is effectively his wife
in effect, they had no choice

senses.definition: in an effective manner
examples: these are real problems that can be dealt with most effectively by rational discussion

senses.definition: capacity to produce strong physiological or chemical effects
examples: the toxin's potency
the strength of the drinks

senses.definition: power to be effective; the quality of being able to bring about an effect
skillfulness in avoiding wasted time and effort
examples: she did the work with great efficiency

senses.definition: the ratio of the output to the input of any system
able to accomplish a purpose; functioning effectively
examples: people who will do nothing unless they get something out of it for themselves are often highly effective persons …
effective personnel
an efficient secretary
the efficient cause of the revolution

senses.definition: being effective without wasting time or effort or expense
examples: an efficient production manager
efficient engines save gas

senses.definition: a notable achievement
examples: he performed a great feat
the book was her finest effort

senses.definition: a series of actions advancing a principle or tending toward a particular end
examples: he supported populist campaigns
they worked in the cause of world peace
the team was ready for a drive toward the pennant
the movement to end slavery
contributed to the war effort

senses.definition: earnest and conscientious activity intended to do or accomplish something
examples: made an effort to cover all the reading material
wished him luck in his endeavor
she gave it a good try

senses.definition: use of physical or mental energy; hard work
examples: he got an A for effort
they managed only with great exertion

senses.definition: not showing effort or strain
examples: a difficult feat performed with casual mastery
casual grace

senses.definition: requiring or apparently requiring no effort
examples: the swallows glided in an effortless way through the busy air
